newsitem.title: USA: NZ's Birch says Brash has achieved NZ dollar goal.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch says Brash has achieved NZ dollar goal.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch played down Don Brash's latest call for a lower exchange rate and high interest rates saying the Reserve Bank Governor had already achieved that goal.
"I think he's achieved pretty much what he set out to achieve ... since he started to make that statement," Mr Birch told Reuters here on Thursday.
"We've seen a slight rebalancing between interest rates and the exchange rate," he said.
Birch also rejected Brash's recent proposal for capital gains tax on property investment.
"We have no proposal for a capital gains tax," he told Reuters.
Earlier this week Brash told Reuters Financial TV in London that he would like a new mix of lower foreign exchange rates and higher interest rates to take the economy forward.

The finance minister who was in New York on Thursday for discussion with Wall Street banks and credit rating agencies said the main difficulty for exporters had been the volatility in U.S. dollar-yen cross rates.
"But with the (New Zealand) Trade-Weighted Index we have seen a relative stability since the beginning of this year," he added.

When asked if a further softening of the exchange rate was desirable Birch said: "It increases their (exporters') competitiveness, but what is important is that we have a clean market operation and the price will be set by the purchasers and sellers of the NZ dollar."

Earlier the minister, answering a question from an audience of business and finance leaders at a New York luncheon, bluntly ruled out the Reserve Bank Governor's capital gains tax proposal saying it would not come under consideration by the government.
